rules: Address the user informally with 'ty' (second person singular verbs). Never use 'Pan' / 'Pani' / 'Państwo'. Prefer leaving the pronoun out when the verb form already makes it clear ('Możesz zmienić...', not 'Ty możesz zmienić...').
Personal and possessive pronouns referring to the user always start with a capital letter: 'Ty', 'Ciebie', 'Cię', 'Ci', 'Twój', 'Twoje', 'Twojego', etc.

Use gender-neutral phrasing for the user — the user's gender is unknown. Never use past-tense verbs ending in '-łeś' / '-łaś' / '-łbyś' or adjectives and participles describing the user ('gotowy', 'zmęczony', 'wdzięczny', 'pewny', 'zalogowany', 'sam'). Rephrase with the present tense, an impersonal form, a noun, or a question about the thing rather than the person: 'Za dużo wyboru?' (not 'Zmęczony wyborem?'), 'po przejściu na nowe konto' (not 'jeśli przeszedłeś na nowe konto'), 'coś, za co czujesz wdzięczność' (not 'za co jesteś wdzięczny'), 'od dwóch tygodni nie palisz?' (not 'rzuciłeś palenie?'), 'Zapisano' (not 'Zapisałeś').
Buttons and menu items use the imperative ('Zapisz', 'Edytuj folder', 'Anuluj').
Address the user informally with 'du' ('dein', 'dich'). Never use 'Sie'.
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Speichern', 'Ordner bearbeiten').
Join compounds with English loanwords using a hyphen ('Plugin-Einstellungen', 'Widget-Konfiguration'), never write them as two separate words.
Compound brand names are fully hyphenated ('Anori-Plus-Konto').

glossary.icon: 'Icon' (never 'Symbol' for an icon the user picks or uploads)

rules: Address the user formally with 'vous' ('votre', 'vos'). Never use 'tu'.

Prefer phrasing that doesn't assign the user a gender ('Trop de choix ?' rather than 'Fatigué de choisir ?', 'plus rien ne vous empêche de...' rather than 'vous êtes prêt à...'). Don't use inclusive-writing dots ('prêt·e').
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Enregistrer', 'Modifier le dossier').
Put a regular space before ':', ';', '?' and '!' as French typography requires; it is converted to a non-breaking space automatically.

glossary.color scheme: 'apparence' (the light/dark mode setting; never 'palette de couleurs')

rules: Use neutral Latin American Spanish: 'computadora' (not 'ordenador'), 'ustedes' for plural (never 'vosotros'), no voseo.
Address the user informally with 'tú' ('tu', 'te').
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Guardar', 'Editar carpeta').

glossary.to stash a tab: 'apartar' (Tab stash = 'Pestañas apartadas'; never 'guardar', which is Save)

rules: Address the user informally with 'tu' ('ti', 'tuo').
Buttons and menu items use the imperative ('Salva', 'Modifica cartella').

glossary.to stash a tab: 'accantonare' (Tab stash = 'Schede accantonate'; never 'salvare', which is Save, nor 'archiviare')

rules: This is Brazilian Portuguese, not European Portuguese. Use Brazilian vocabulary and spelling throughout.
Address the user with 'você' (never 'tu' or 'o senhor').
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Salvar', 'Editar pasta').
A browser tab is 'guia' (plural 'guias'), never 'aba'. This includes 'nova guia' for the new tab page, 'grupo de guias', and 'Guias' as the name of the Tabs plugin.
For enabling or disabling a feature or setting use 'ativar' / 'desativar' (and 'ativado' / 'desativado'), never 'habilitar' / 'desabilitar'.
The computer mouse is 'mouse', never 'rato'.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'guardar' (Tab stash = 'Guias guardadas'; never 'salvar', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'вы' (lower-case 'вы', 'ваш'). Never use 'ты'.
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Сохранить', 'Редактировать папку').
Use 'ё' consistently.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'отложить' (Tab stash = 'Отложенные вкладки'; never 'сохранить', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'ви' (lower-case 'ви', 'ваш'). Never use 'ти'.
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Зберегти', 'Редагувати папку').
Write the apostrophe inside words as ʼ (U+02BC): 'компʼютер', 'підʼєднати', 'імʼя'.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'відкласти' (Tab stash = 'Відкладені вкладки'; never 'зберегти', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'vy' (lower-case 'vy', 'váš'). Never use 'ty'.

Use gender-neutral phrasing for the user — the user's gender is unknown. In formal address the past participle and predicate adjectives still show gender ('byl jste' / 'byla jste', 'přihlášen' / 'přihlášena', 'připraven', 'unaven', 'vděčný', 'sám'), so never use them about the user. Rephrase with the present tense, a passive or impersonal form, or a noun: 'Přihlášení proběhlo' (not 'Byl jste přihlášen'), 'Příliš mnoho možností?' (not 'Jste unaven z výběru?'), 'Uloženo' (not 'Uložil jste').
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Uložit', 'Upravit složku').
Anori is neuter.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'odložit' (Tab stash = 'Odložené karty'; never 'uložit', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'vy' (lower-case 'vy', 'váš'). Never use 'ty'.
Buttons and menu items use the infinitive ('Uložiť', 'Upraviť priečinok').

glossary.to stash a tab: 'odložiť' (Tab stash = 'Odložené karty'; never 'uložiť', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'siz' (second person plural verb forms, '-iniz' possessives).
Buttons and menu items use the bare imperative ('Kaydet', 'Klasörü düzenle').
Attach suffixes to English loanwords and brand names with an apostrophe ('widget'ı', 'Anori'yi').
Avoid attaching suffixes to {{placeholders}} and $t(...) references — use 'Label: {{value}}' or follow with a separate noun.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'depoya ekle' (Tab stash = 'Sekme deposu'; never 'kaydet', which is Save)

rules: Use polite です/ます forms in sentences; buttons and menu items use short noun or plain forms ('保存', 'フォルダを編集'). Use the standard UI courtesy phrases where natural ('ご覧ください', 'お試しください', 'ご協力ください', 'ご利用いただけます', 'お持ちでない方', 'ご紹介します', '〜していただけると'), as the original native translation does; avoid heavier honorific or humble constructions beyond these set phrases.
Use full-width Japanese punctuation (、。！？) in Japanese text, and put a half-width space between Japanese and Latin-script words ('Anori の設定'). Quotation marks stay straight per the general rule.
Numbers attached to Japanese counters/units take no space ('{{count}}日', '{{hours}}時間{{minutes}}分').
Settings labels and toggles end in a noun rather than a verb ('サイドバーを自動で非表示', 'コンパクトモードに自動切り替え', '結果なし').
Labels showing a value use 'label：value' with a full-width colon ('現在の画面幅：{{screenWidth}}px') rather than a full sentence.
Omitting the subject is fine; never use '私たち' for the solo developer.

glossary.icon: 'アイコン' (custom icons = 'カスタムアイコン')
glossary.to stash a tab: 'ストック' (Tab stash = 'タブストック'; never '保存', which is Save)
glossary.Anki review buttons: match Anki's own Japanese UI: 'もう一度' / '難しい' / '正解' / '簡単'; Show answer = '解答を表示'
glossary.freezing rain / drizzle: '着氷性の雨' / '着氷性の霧雨' (not '凍雨', which means ice pellets)

rules: Address the user with '你' (never '您').

Use full-width Chinese punctuation (，。！？：) in Chinese text, and put a half-width space between Chinese characters and Latin-script words or numbers ('Anori 不会', '10 分钟'). Quotation marks stay straight per the general rule. Don't add a trailing full stop to buttons, labels or titles.
Separate list items with '、' and clauses with '，'.
In mock content (example tasks, posts), localize jokes to relatable Chinese everyday humour rather than translating them literally.

glossary.widget: '小部件' (as the original native translation uses)

rules: Address the user as 'bạn'.

glossary.widget: 'widget' (never 'tiện ích' — that word means a browser extension)
glossary.to stash a tab: 'cất' (Tab stash = 'Kho tab'; never 'lưu', which is Save)

rules: Address the user formally with 'Anda' (capitalized). Never use 'kamu' or 'kau'.

glossary.to stash a tab: 'sisihkan' (Tab stash = 'Tab disisihkan'; never 'simpan', which is Save)

rules: Use a formal register. Address the user with 'kayo' / 'ninyo' / 'inyo' (never 'ikaw' / 'mo' / 'iyo'), without adding 'po'.
Keep technical terms that have no established Filipino equivalent in English, spelled as in English; don't transliterate them.
Address the user formally with 'आप'.
Write English loanwords in Devanagari, never in Latin script ('एनालिटिक्स', not 'analytics'). Brand names (Anori, Anori Plus, GitHub) stay in Latin script.
End sentences with '।'.
Use nuqta (फ़, ज़) consistently.
Address the user as 'คุณ'. Don't use gendered polite particles (ครับ / ค่ะ).

glossary.keyboard shortcut: 'แป้นพิมพ์ลัด'
glossary.icon: 'ไอคอน' (custom icons = 'ไอคอนที่กำหนดเอง')
glossary.to stash a tab: 'เก็บ' (Tab stash = 'ที่เก็บแท็บ'; Save = 'บันทึก')
glossary.notes: 'โน้ต' (not 'บันทึกย่อ', which clashes with Save)
glossary.the onboarding's ready-made setup: 'การจัดหน้าพร้อมใช้'
glossary.the developer's 'I': 'ผม', but prefer phrasing without a pronoun

rules: Use Modern Standard Arabic. Address the user with gender-neutral phrasing where possible (e.g. verbal nouns instead of gendered imperatives); fall back to the masculine form only when unavoidable.
Use Western digits (0-9).
Keep brand names (Anori, Anori Plus, GitHub) in Latin script; never transliterate them into Arabic.
Write file formats as 'PNG' etc. without leading dots.
Write without short-vowel diacritics (harakat); only fathatan on alif (ًا) is used.
Buttons, menu items, settings labels and shortcut descriptions are verbal nouns ('حفظ', 'تحرير المجلد', 'إظهار/إخفاء'); progress labels use 'جار + verbal noun...' ('جار التحميل...').

glossary.to stash a tab: 'تخبئة' (Tab stash = 'مخبأ علامات التبويب'; never 'حفظ', which is Save)
